subject: Recap: Private VPC deployment options & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmerobotics.com>, Jenny Liu <jenny.liu@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Private VPC deployment options & next steps

Hi Daniel / Jenny —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can move the Private VPC evaluation forward.

High-level ask (from your side):
- Must keep inference traffic inside Acme-owned VPCs; no public internet access for model requests.
- Audit logs & 90-day retention for request/response metadata (non-PHI).
- Low-latency requirement for interactive use (~100–150ms p50 token latency target).
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~50 requests/sec with occasional bursts to 200.

Deployment options we discussed:
- Hosted API (not acceptable due to data residency/isolation)
- Dedicated capacity (good fit if isolation + managed infra suffice)
- Private VPC (preferred) — options: AWS VPC Peering vs PrivateLink, or cloud-interconnect for on-prem.

Open items / network inputs we need from you to recommend final architecture:
- Preferred connection type: VPC Peering or PrivateLink? (you mentioned PrivateLink was preferred on the call)
- Cloud provider & region(s) (AWS us-west-2 confirmed?)
- VPC ID(s), CIDR block(s), and a list of subnets you can allow (app/public/private).
- Do you require static outbound IPs from Redwood for firewall allowlist, or will you accept PrivateLink with ALB and TLS?
- Point of contact for networking (name/email/availability) — we suggested a 30–45 minute tech call next week with your network engineer and our infra lead.

Attachments: I attached our initial VPC design draft and a short checklist to capture the items above.

Next steps (proposal):
1) You share the CIDRs / preferred connection approach and network contact (by Wed 4/21)
2) Tech call with our infra engineer (Sean) to nail down peering/PrivateLink details (target: Thu 4/22)
3) Exchange any firewall allowlist IPs and test account info post-call

If PrivateLink is the path, we’ll need your account ID/ALB configuration and we’ll prepare a CloudFormation template + test runbook. If peering, we’ll ask for peering authorization details and route table guidance.

Thanks — happy to adjust timing to match your team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
- We prefer PrivateLink for the security model (avoid adding routes across accounts).
- Cloud: AWS us-west-2 (primary).
- VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h, CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16.
- Allowed subnets: 10.10.1.0/24 (app servers), 10.10.2.0/24 (ingress/load balancer).
- We will need a set of static IPs (or NATed egress) for our firewall — if PrivateLink is used we can rely on the ALB endpoint but would still like a small set of IPs for allowlisting.

Networking POC: Jenny Liu (jenny.liu@acmerobotics.com). She’s available Thu 4/22 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 4/23 morning.

I attached our firewall allowlist template and a brief topology doc. Happy to join the tech call to walk through.

Thanks,
Daniel

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmerobotics.com>, Jenny Liu <jenny.liu@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Private VPC deployment options & next steps

Hi all — looping in a few technical clarifications from the Redwood infra side before the call: 

1) PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink is fine and usually simpler for security teams. For PrivateLink we'll create a cross-account NLB/ALB in our account and provide a VPC endpoint service name. We need your account ID and the subnet IDs where you want the interface endpoints provisioned.

2) Static IPs: If you require a fixed egress IP for upstream firewall allowlisting, we can provision an outbound NAT through a small egress fleet in your VPC (via peering) or provide a set of stable IPs via our NLB in front of the PrivateLink endpoint. Which would you prefer?

3) Ports/Protocols: All traffic is TLS (443). We do not require additional ports. We will present a minimal set of security group rules for the endpoint.

4) Cross-account IAM: For peering we need peering accept permissions in your account; for PrivateLink we only need endpoint creation on your side. Please confirm your team's preference and whether we should prepare a CloudFormation/terraform snippet.

5) Test plan: recommend a canary flow — create a test service and run 1k test requests over 24 hours to validate latency and egress behavior before cutover.

I'll be on the call Thu 4/22 at 10:00 PT if that works. If you pick PrivateLink, please share: account ID, preferred subnet IDs, and any IP allowlist constraints.

Thanks — Sean
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
